sections.body: Citation mapping and discovery is the study of how research papers connect through references, shared ideas, and patterns of use. In practice, AI systems build citation graphs, group papers by meaning, and trace how a finding moves from one field to another. They do not just count links, they read titles, abstracts, and full text to infer why one paper cites another. This site's library holds 135 research papers, so the work here is grounded in a bounded collection rather than the whole literature. The aim is to help a reader see structure in a body of work, not to replace reading the original papers. The pages in this section show different views of that structure.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are well solved. Citation graphs over time are straightforward to build when metadata is clean, and clustering papers by meaning works well enough to surface obvious groups. What is not solved is intent: a citation can be supportive, critical, or merely conventional, and automated systems still struggle to tell these apart reliably. Bridge studies are harder still, because a paper that connects two fields may look marginal in both. Trend forecasting is the least settled, since early signals are noisy and many predicted trends never materialize. The honest limit is that these tools produce candidates and patterns for a human to inspect, not final judgments about influence or quality.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader can start with Citation Graphs Over Time to see how links accumulate and shift across a literature. Clustering Papers by Meaning then groups those papers by topic rather than by explicit reference, which helps when citation links are sparse. How a Paper Is Cited goes deeper into the local context of a single citation, separating background mention from substantive use. Bridge Studies Between Fields looks at papers that sit between communities and often carry ideas across boundaries. Forecasting Research Trends uses the same graph and cluster signals to project where attention may move next, with all the uncertainty that implies. Together these pages move from structure to meaning to prediction, and each one points back to the original paper rather than to a search tool.
